extracted.intended_audience: Immigrants and children of immigrants applying to the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans (prospective 2027 applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Official eligibility and program requirements for applicants to the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans (2027 cycle), including definitions of New American status, academic/enrollment requirements, program obligations, financial rules, and allowed application exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must be 30 or younger as of the application deadline. There is no minimum age requirement. Do not expect exceptions: 'Do you make exceptions to the age requirements? No. In order to be fair to all applicants we make no exceptions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: New American status — general definition
rubrics_metrics.description: You are a New American — an immigrant or the child of immigrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are an immigrant, you should be a naturalized US citizen, a green card holder, an asylee or refugee, or someone who graduated from both high school and college in the United States. Your birth parents must have both been born outside of the US as non-US citizens, and both parents must not have been eligible for US citizenship at the time of their births. Parents' current immigration status or location is not relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: New American — US citizen by birth special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a US citizen by birth then additional conditions apply for New American eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one of the following must be true: (a) Both of your birth parents were born abroad as non-US citizens and were not eligible for US citizenship at the time of their births; (b) You were raised by only one of your birth parents, the parent that raised you was born abroad as a non-US citizen, and your second birth parent was not a part of your life growing up and you have no contact with them; (c) You were born in the United States and both of your biological parents were born abroad as non-US citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: New American — born abroad / immigration-status categories
rubrics_metrics.description: If you were born abroad as a non-US citizen, eligibility can be satisfied through several categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable categories include: Naturalized Citizen (naturalized on your own or as a minor under a parent's application); Adopted (born outside US and subsequently adopted by American parents and awarded US citizenship due to adoption); Green Card (possession of a valid green card); Refugee & Asylees (granted asylum or refugee status). If none of these apply, eligibility may still be possible if you graduated from both high school and college in the US (this includes current and past DACA recipients).

rubrics_metrics.name: DACA and graduated-in-US pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduated from High School and College in the US pathway
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of the other categories apply and you were born abroad, you must have graduated from both high school and college in the US to be eligible. DACA recipients who were born abroad and graduated from both high school and college in the US are explicitly eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for New American/naturalization (application stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are not required to submit supporting naturalization documentation at initial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are asked to provide the date they received their documentation. Supporting documentation will be requested if you reach the finalist stage. (If having trouble with naturalization documentation, PD Soros no longer requires submission at initial application.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic degree requirement (by Fellowship start)
rubrics_metrics.description: You will have a bachelor’s degree as of the fall of 2027 when the 2027 Fellowship begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may have a previous graduate degree. Applicants must be planning to be enrolled in a full-time degree-granting graduate or professional program in the United States in the 2027-2028 academic year. Online programs are eligible for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment timing and admissions status
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply before being admitted to graduate school, but must plan to be enrolled full-time in the 2027-28 year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many applicants apply to PD Soros at the same time they apply to graduate school. If applying in fall 2026 for the 2027 Fellowship you should be planning to be enrolled full-time in fall 2027 and spring 2028. The first year of the Fellowship cannot be deferred; year two may be deferred up to one calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current graduate students: year-limit rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are already in graduate school when you apply, you must not have started the third year of the degree program you are seeking funding for as of the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot have started a third or subsequent year of that program as of the deadline. For joint- or dual-degree programs, the program you are enrolled in for 2027-28 must meet the eligibility requirements. Special cases (e.g., integrated master’s/PhD programs) are evaluated based on whether the degrees are distinct programs or one continuous program; if the master’s and PhD are considered one program and the master’s was two years, year one of the PhD may count as year three of the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain program types are explicitly ineligible for PD Soros funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ineligible: Executive graduate programs; joint bachelors/master’s programs in which both degrees are awarded simultaneously; certificate programs; post-baccalaureate programs; graduate programs that are not in the United States; graduate programs that are not fully accredited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedural rules and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Application deadline and selection process timeline for the 2027 fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2027 application due October 29, 2026 at 2 pm ET. Applications are not reviewed until after the deadline. After review the top 77 applicants will be designated 'finalists' and asked to appear for virtual interviews in late January and early February 2027. 30 of the 77 finalists will be selected as Fellows and notified in March 2027; Fellows will be announced publicly in April 2027 and fellowship funding begins fall 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-exceptions / no-extensions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PD Soros enforces fairness policies regarding deadlines and age requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect extensions on deadlines: 'Do you grant extensions? No, in order to be fair to all applicants we do not grant any extensions.' Age exceptions are also not made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-application policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who are not selected may re-apply if they continue to meet eligibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yes, you can re-apply as long as you still fit the eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship obligations during award year
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements Fellows must meet during their two-year Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are required to attend the annual Fall Conference in New York City (paid by program). The director or deputy director will visit each Fellow on campus during the first fall semester. Fellows should not work full-time during their graduate program; they are required to remain in good standing in their graduate program while receiving funding. At the close of two years, Fellows must submit an exit report. More details provided in contract when selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial terms, caps, and interactions with other awards
rubrics_metrics.description: PD Soros stipend and tuition policies, and how they interact with other awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD Soros pays 50% of tuition and fees (not including health and housing fees), up to $10,000 per semester or $6,667 per quarter. If a Fellow is receiving other funding for tuition or 50% of tuition is less than the maximum, the Fellow will not receive the maximum tuition funding. PD Soros cannot exceed tuition and fees cost and tuition funds cannot be reallocated as stipend. The maximum PD Soros stipend is $25,000 per year, capping all stipend awards at $50,000 per year. A Fellow can receive up to $25,000 in stipend per year from sources other than the Fellowship; if the Fellow receives over $25,000 in stipend from other sources, PD Soros will reduce their stipend payment to fall within the $50,000 cap. PD Soros does not limit the number of awards a student can receive simultaneously; they coordinate with other awards to maximize benefit within other awards' limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional exhibits: allowed content and authorship guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on optional exhibit uploads and how to represent collaborative work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can submit an exhibit made with others but should provide context on why you are including it and your contribution. For technical works (research papers, comment letters) you may submit an abstract/summary, an excerpt, the whole paper, or a link. It can be helpful to include a sentence or two about why you included an exhibit and what it shows about you; if obvious, this may not be necessary. Brief descriptions can be uploaded as separate documents or on each exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials guidance (transcripts, school listing, program lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical instructions for filling application fields and supplying transcripts/exhibits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcripts: submit even if you have no grades yet—the transcript will show courses you are enrolled in and validate attendance. Schools: if your school is not listed, select 'other' and type its name. Programs: There are only four program spaces on the application — list the four schools/programs you are most likely to attend and upload a full list as an exhibit if needed.
